# Combine all data
all_outlays = outlays_1984 + outlays_1985 + outlays_1986 + outlays_1987

print(f"Total months: {len(all_outlays)}")
print(f"Outlays: {all_outlays}")

# Calculate geometric mean
# GM = (product of all values)^(1/n)
product = 1
for val in all_outlays:

geometric_mean = product ** (1/len(all_outlays))
print(f"\nGeometric mean: {geometric_mean}")
print(f"Geometric mean (rounded to thousandths): {round(geometric_mean, 3)}")

from functools import reduce
import math

# Monthly judiciary outlays from Jan 1984 to Mar 1987 (in millions)
outlays = [84, 89, 63, 74, 62, 93, 65, 79, 69, 79, 67, 96,  # 1984
           66, 60, 59, 119, 75, 63, 74, 103, 66, 98, 74, 102,  # 1985
           76, 109, 74, 129, 75, 71, 70, 106, 87, 73, 73, 113,  # 1986
           79, 76, 110]  # 1987 Jan-Mar

# Using math.prod for Python 3.8+
product = math.prod(outlays)
print(f"Product: {product}")

geometric_mean = product ** (1/len(outlays))
print(f"Geometric mean: {geometric_mean}")
print(f"Rounded to 3 decimal places: {round(geometric_mean, 3)}")

# Alternative calculation using logarithms
log_sum = sum(math.log(x) for x in outlays)
gm_alt = math.exp(log_sum / len(outlays))
print(f"GM via logs: {gm_alt}")
EOF
